checked.description: Whether the box is ticked. Bound to the control BOTH ways, and each binding answers a different question. The PROPERTY is the live state: once the reader clicks, the checkedness dirty flag is set and the content attribute stops controlling the box, so a property binding is the only one that keeps tracking a host write after the first click. The content ATTRIBUTE is the control's DEFAULT checkedness, and it is mirrored because this element is not form-associated (specs/ui.md 3.2): it never hears form.reset(), so without the mirror a reset would move the CONTROL to the authored default and leave the element's state where it was, and the two would disagree silently. With it, a reset is a visible no-op, which is a missing feature rather than a lie.

indeterminate.description: The mixed state: neither ticked nor clear, for a box standing over a set that is partly on. HTML gives it no content attribute at all — it exists only as a property — which is the reason this element exists: written into attributes it would parse, validate and silently do nothing. So there is nothing to mirror and no default for a form reset to return to, and a click clears it in the platform.

disabled.description: Cannot be ticked or focused. Disabled, never absent.

label.description: The accessible name, forwarded to the control as aria-label. Leave it empty when the slotted text is on screen: the empty value REMOVES the attribute so the wrapping label's text names the box, rather than naming it twice.

labelledby.description: Forwarded to the inner control as aria-labelledby, for a visible label the box does not wrap.

describedby.description: Forwarded to the inner control as aria-describedby, for a help or error sentence the row owns.

name.description: The form field name, forwarded to the control.

size.description: sm, md or lg. The row height is the kit's, so a column of controls lines up.

tabindex.description: Forwarded to the inner control as its tabindex, which is what makes a roving caret possible: the focusable node is the input inside, not the host and not the label that wraps it, so a jx-toolbar moving focus writes this rather than reaching into a child's internals. It is a PROPERTY ONLY (el.tabindex = "0") and deliberately not an observed attribute: written as an attribute it would land on the host as well, and a host carrying tabindex is itself focusable, so the one control would become two tab stops.

onChange.description: Mirrors both halves of the control's state back. A click on a mixed box clears indeterminate and toggles checked in the platform; reading only checked would let the next flush re-assert mixed over the reader's own tick. The native change and input events bubble from the control as they always do.
